item.title: Bill Cowher calls for Browns to commit to Shedeur Sanders
item.description: Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images, CBS The Cleveland Browns have gotten off to a better start to the NFL season than anyone expected . The longtime basement dwellers of the league were 5–3 heading into Sunday’s showdown on the road against the New Orleans Saints. Cleveland had to make one significant change to the lineup before their game on Sunday, with backup quarterback Shedeur Sanders stepping up to start due to Deshaun Watson missing the week’s worth of practice while in the league’s concussion protocol. The Browns ultimately lost to the Saints 23–22 in overtime, but Sanders showed enough skill to have Browns fans excited for what could be in store for their young quarterback, and even convinced some analysts that it was time for Cleveland to embrace the future. Speaking after the game, former Steelers coach Bill Cowher was adamant that the Browns should commit to Sanders under center full time, even if Watson were to be available next week. “I would just say this: Moving forward, Shedeur Sanders should be the starter for this football team,” Cowher said. “He’s going to be the future. And I think what he showed today, his resilience, continued to come back. He made great decisions, he extended plays. I love the way he played and I would move forward with him.” When cohost Nate Burleson asked if Cowher believed Watson hadn’t played well enough to get his job back when healthy, Cowher said it was more important to look into the future. “One person’s unfortunate situation creates another person’s opportunity. I just think that right now, what I saw from Shedeur Sanders, I would move forward. Because he is the future of your football team.” “Shedeur Sanders should be the starter for this football team. He’s gonna be the future.” – Bill Cowher https://t.co/UN78KLHXxX — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 8, 2026 While it might sound odd for a team to consider starting its 0–1 backup quarterback over its 5–3 starting quarterback when both are healthy, the game that Sanders played on Sunday showed why it might be worth looking into for the Browns. Sanders finished the game 297 passing yards, two touchdowns, and zero interceptions. His QB rating was 114.6 on the day. In Watson’s eight starts this season, he’s cleared 270 yards passing just twice, thrown for two touchdowns just twice, and has never done both in the same game. Just one of his eight starts saw him record a QB rating in the triple digits. Further, Sanders was able to deliver in crunch time when the Browns needed him, creating space and throwing an impressive pass in the final minute to put his team in position to kick a game-tying field goal to force overtime. This play alone is better than anything Watson has done all year. Keep developing Shedeur. He’s the future. https://t.co/6udkhpSyqk — Brownies (@BrowniesToBowl) November 8, 2026 Beyond his play on the field, there’s plenty more extremely simple reasons the Browns might want to get a head start on the potential Sanders era.

item.title: Patriots QB Drake Maye’s brutally honest self-assessment after Packers loss is on point
item.description: Credit: David Butler II-Imagn Images Patriots QB Drake Maye’s brutally honest self-assessment after Packers loss is on point appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New England Patriots lost 45-27 at Gillette Stadium, hitting a new historic low against the Packers . Maye linked up with Tom Brady for an incredible photo but didn’t play quite up to the five-time Super Bowl champion’s standards in a losing effort. Maye was asked about his performance after the game in comments shared by Mike Reiss of ESPN NFL Nation. “Yeah, very…I’m disappointed in myself…We had (chances) to get back in the game, messed ’em up. We had a chance to get back to within three points multiple times, just frustrating. I’ve gotta do a better job from the whole perspective, I wasn’t good today, we gotta bounce back, and know that this was the game’s lesson, we’re battling.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Maye passed for 299 yards and three touchdowns, but his three interceptions stood out like a sore thumb on a day when New England coughed the football up four times compared to zero for Matt LaFleur’s Packers. Maye’s team converted 4-of-9 third downs but also gave up four sacks and fell behind the eight-ball by a score of 14-0 after one quarter. Coach Mike Vrabel ’s Patriots seem content to stand pat with the team they have heading toward Tuesday, November 10’s trade deadline, but there seems to be a lot missing with New England right now and AJ Brown’s injury absence is just one part of it. TreVeyon Henderson’s absence isn’t helping, either, but the Patriots have to play better football regardless of their starting lineup, and Maye knows it. item.title: After joining OKC, Nique Clifford pens goodbye message to Kings: 'Truly blessed'
item.description: Continuing to shuffle their duct-taped roster, the Oklahoma City Thunder added another piece to fortify their depth. They acquired Nique Clifford from the Sacramento Kings for two future second-round picks. This signals another buy-low move on cheap, cost-controlled young talent. In his second season, Clifford had fallen out of favor with the Kings. He was outside of their rotation. That's after a surprisingly-productive rookie year. He's averaged 7.9 points on 41.6% shooting, 3.5 rebounds and 2.3 assists in his career. He was the No. 24 pick of the 2025 NBA draft. Only 83 games into his NBA career, Clifford has experienced the cold-hearted business side of things. His time on the Kings was short — specifically, for a first-round pick. But now, he gets a fresh opportunity on the Thunder. The 24-year-old said his goodbyes to Sacramento after the trade was made official. Clifford wrote on his Instagram story: "Thank you Sac for everything in my short time here! Truly blessed for all the experiences and memories. Wish I could've done more for yall" Clifford then flipped the page to the next chapter of his NBA journey with the Thunder. It'll be interesting to see where he falls in OKC's rotation. The defense-first forward should add to that side of the ball, but his career 32.6% 3-point shot suggests the offense is still a work in progress — and a negative, if you're cynical. Obviously, Clifford will need time to adjust to his new NBA home and role. He goes from the worst team in the league to a recent NBA champion and constant title contender. Season-altering injuries to Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren and Cason Wallace have shaken things up a bit. This deal is the latest example of that ripple effect. item.title: 📹 After exit, coach sees a way for Vasco to be great again
item.description: 📹 After exit, coach sees a way for Vasco to be great again This Sunday (8), Vasco fans suffered yet another disappointment this season. After their traumatic elimination from the CONMEBOL Sudamericana against Boca Juniors at a packed Maracanã, the Cruz-Maltino also crashed out of the Copa do Brasil semifinals, this time against Palmeiras on penalties at São Januário. Speaking in the press room afterward, coach Pedro Emanuel expressed pride in Vasco's run in the tournament. The 51-year-old Portuguese coach, who joined the Gigante da Colina in July this year and is under contract until December 2027, stressed that frustrating exits like those Vasco suffered this season are part of the rebuilding process for "teams that were once great and want to be great again" . "Football is as magical as it is cruel. And today was a cruel day for us. It could have been magical. We were seconds away from it being magical for us. It was magical for Palmeiras and cruel for us. What I take away from this Copa (do Brasil) is pride in our journey and the way we went out. Together with our fans, we built up great expectations for this competition. It's an important competition, and we knew that and wanted to deliver that for them. And I think, in the end, when we all left the pitch, we felt sad because we really did everything within our power to reach the final. And today was a true final. There was a very capable, very talented team on the other side. And this is also part of the growth of teams like Vasco, who were once great and want to be great again. This is the path we have to follow." Pedro Emanuel also made a point of recalling an interview with Arsenal's Brazilian defender Gabriel Magalhães, who noted that the Gunners had to settle for second place for four consecutive seasons before becoming Premier League champions again. "Today (Sunday), I saw the comments from Arsenal defender Gabriel (Magalhães). He said they finished runners-up four times in England and managed to find the formula to win on the fifth attempt." item.title: Studs and duds from Houston’s 44-22 win against the Chargers
item.description: The Houston Texans put up their best performance of the season in their 44-22 win against the Los Angeles Chargers. Houston’s offense look unstoppable, going three for four in the red zone and scoring five touchdowns. Los Angeles also turned the ball over twice, which helped the Texans get this victory. You could tell from the first drive of the game that Houston was going to have a good day offensively. The 7th-ranked passing attack marched down the field in eight plays, going 73 yards for their first touchdown of the night. Quarterback CJ Stroud had one blemish in the second quarter when he threw an interception, but was otherwise near-perfect, throwing for a season-high 386 yards and tying his career-best with five touchdown passes. Defensively, they disrupted the Chargers’ offense all game with eight sacks and two takeaways. Through the first three quarters, Los Angeles only had nine points. They ended up benching their quarterback, Justin Herbert, before the end of the game. Here are the studs and duds from Houston’s third win of the season, including Stroud who threw a career-high five touchdown passes in this win and wide receiver Kayshon Boutte who had a career-high 125 receiving yards. Stud: QB C.J. Stroud Coming into this game, the Los Angeles Chargers were supposed to be a top-10 passing defense, but CJ Stroud completely shredded them. Los Angeles only allowed eight passing touchdowns in the first seven games, but Stroud had five passing touchdowns, tying his career-high. There was no stopping Stroud and the passing offense in this game. This just added to Stroud’s great performance this season. Dud: RB Woody Marks It is not like Houston needed to run the ball, but the offense was hoping to exploit Los Angeles’ statistically poor run defense. Instead, the run was barely able to get over 100 yards. Woody Marks only had 70 rushing yards, averaging 3.9 yards per attempt, including two runs over 10 yards. This is not terrible, but they need more out of the run game going forward and Marks is probably going to be the answer since David Montgomery was not doing much before his injury. Stud: WR Kayshon Boutte Boutte was essentially a non-factor for Houston’s offense before the bye week. But in this game, he emerged as the Texans’ leading receiver with four receptions for 125 yards and two touchdowns. It was just his third career game with at least 100 yards. His 63-yard touchdown was tied with Tank Dell’s touchdown earlier in the game for Houston’s longest touchdown of the season. Dud: WR Marvin Harrison Jr The Texans had an offensive explosion against the Chargers, especially in the passing game. However, Harrison was barely involved. He was only targeted three times and had two receptions for 20 yards. This was really disappointing after scoring a touchdown in Houston’s last game. Still, not everyone can get targets, so maybe this just was not his week. Perhaps Harrison will get more touches next week against the Cleveland Browns. Stud: WR

item.title: LeBron James’ Statement On His Family’s Safety After Arrested Stalker Claims To Be His Son
item.description: Nov 8, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James (23) reacts and celebrates a three point shot against the Chicago Bulls during the second half at United Center. Mandatory Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images A man was recently arrested for allegedly stalking LeBron James’ LA home and claiming to be his son after trespassing on the property. The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Chicago Bulls 127-121 tonight after a nail-biting matchup that was decided in the closing stretch of the game. James finished with 22 points, five rebounds, and five assists while shooting 8-16 from the field (50.0% FG) and 2-5 from behind the three-point line (40.0% 3P). Following the win, LeBron James spoke to the media scrum in the locker room and addressed the reported arrest. “My family is safe, and that’s the most important. We’re still looking into everything,” James said in the 76ers’ locker room. According to TMZ, the suspect was caught while seemingly trespassing on LeBron James’ property when the star or his family were not at home. “Law enforcement sources tell TMZ, security called the cops around 9 PM Friday after catching a male suspect on the property on one of their security cameras. After the LAPD showed up, they arrested the alleged suspect for stalking,” TMZ reported. “Oddly enough, the suspect claimed to believe he is LeBron’s son during his chat with cops. Thankfully, LeBron wasn’t home at the time as LBJ was playing with the 76ers against the Cleveland Cavaliers in Ohio. We’re told the suspect didn’t make entry into the residence and that a police report for stalking was taken,” they concluded . This comes after a string of robberies has been observed that have targeted athletes over the past few years. But while the alleged stalker did not manage to get inside the building, his presence created a fear of potential robbery as well. So it is natural for LeBron James to worry mainly about his family’s safety before considering baseless or outrageous claims like having a fourth child. LeBron James has three children with his wife, Savannah James, namely Bronny, Bryce, and Zhuri James. And while there is no proof that anything the stalker claims is true, we live in a generation where information not directly refuted becomes fact for most people. Therefore, James should be encouraged to directly refute any of the stalker’s claims. In the end, James stated unequivocally that his family’s safety is still his top priority as things develop. The intrusion into the NBA superstar’s private property is the more worrisome issue, even though his outrageous claims have garnered attention. Hopefully, going forward, Los Angeles authorities can guarantee James and his family’s safety.

item.description: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 08: Christian McCaffrey #23 of the San Francisco 49ers runs the ball against the Las Vegas Raiders during the first quarter at Levi's Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) Getty The San Francisco 49ers are back from their bye week and facing the Las Vegas Raiders at Levi’s Stadium on Sunday afternoon. Even with several key players, including Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Christian Kirk, sidelined, the 49ers offense didn’t miss a beat in the first half. Much of that success came from the dominance of running back Christian McCaffrey. McCaffrey serves as a workhorse in the backfield as a runner, but he’s also a safety blanket for quarterback Brock Purdy as a pass catcher. 49ers Make Announcement on McCaffrey San Francisco took a 21-10 lead into halftime, and McCaffrey made some NFL history during the first two quarters. He rushed 13 times for 56 yards and a touchdown while adding one reception for 12 yards and another touchdown through the air. That performance put him in an exclusive category of his own. After McCaffrey scored his second touchdown, the 49ers announced that he now holds the record for the most receiving touchdowns by a running back in the Super Bowl era. “He’s sitting at the top,” the 49ers posted on X. item.title: Another QB injury: Drew Lock’s status ‘up in the air’ for Week 10 vs. Raiders
item.description: It might be Jalen Milroe time for the Seattle Seahawks. While Drew Lock didn’t miss any game action during Seattle’s 17-3 win over the Arizona Cardinals, he has a new injury on top of the severe tendinitis he reportedly had been battling over the past couple of weeks. Lock was seen grabbing his right hip area during the third quarter of Sunday’s game, grimacing and walking gingerly as he got off the field prior to Seattle’s final scoring drive. Jalen Milroe warmed up on the sidelines while Lock went into the blue tent, but Lock stayed in for the rest of the afternoon and didn’t miss a play. Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald told reporters at the post-game press conference that Lock’s status is “up in the air” after getting his oblique looked at. “We’re looking at him for an oblique, so we’ll assess it and go from there,” Macdonald said. “He made it out [of the game], but you know, like I’ve sat here before and told you a guy would be ready and then he wasn’t. So, leave my options open.” For what it’s worth, Lock said “we’ll get it looked at [Sunday night]” and that it “was not too bad.” When asked if the injury affected him, he said, “I wouldn’t say it did.” The Seahawks talk about having a “70-man roster,” knowing they’ll frequently need contributions from beyond the 53. With six starters down, this was one of those weeks. Mike Macdonald said it showed “the power of our 70” and called Drew Lock “a beast” for playing through injury. pic.twitter.com/rp7ZM3vgeo — Brady Henderson (@BradyHenderson) November 9, 2026 Lock also said he felt “good” playing through the elbow injury. Odds are not sounding favorable for Sam Darnold to return against the Las Vegas Raiders, with ESPN’s Adam Schefter reporting what felt like a pretty obvious situation that he is in “jeopardy” of missing Week 10 with quad and rib injuries. If Darnold was listed as “week-to-week” by Mike Macdonald, this isn’t earth-shattering news as much as it affirms what’s already been said. If the news is negative on Lock, then we could see Jalen Milroe’s first career NFL start. But at the minimum, this is a very banged up Seahawks quarterback room and the bye week might be one of the most welcome byes in recent Seahawks history.

item.title: Barcelona move clear at the top after Fermín López’s double stuns Atlético Madrid
item.description: They had been in a battle, they had been behind and they had been on edge, but Barcelona found a way through, holding on to their place at the top of the table and holding the doubts at bay for another day. A fortnight in which they were defeated by Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid , in which they might have wondered if something was not right, ended with a 2-1 win at Atlético Madrid. This was a proper test and a proper game, 10 World Cup winners on the field and first place awaiting the winner, and at the end of an intense enjoyable night, that was Hansi Flick’s side. At a noisy Metropolitano, the atmosphere matching the occasion, against a frenetic Atlético side that went for the throat, Barcelona trailed to a Giuliano Simeone goal and for a while in a frenzied first half it looked like there may be no way back. But they found it, two goals from Fermín López either side of the break leading them to the kind of victory that brings a reward beyond the points. It hadn’t been easy but they had made it; ultimately, they might conclude they had found a way to manage it too, some satisfaction in the suffering, in how they resisted and re-established control amid the chaos. After winning their first seven games of the season, Manchester City’s 3-1 loss at Nottingham Forest extended their poor run. Jair Cunha dispossessed Josko Gvardiol to score the opener, then Liam Delap struck twice with muscular surges on the break as Forest won their first home league game since April. “Today I think [the problem] has been general,” said Maresca. “It’s not about one player. In the first half we lost all the duels, all the contacts. Against this team, that is fighting relegation, if you don’t match them … it’s something we need to understand. In this kind of game, if you’re not able to win duels and second balls like in the first half, you struggle. Continue reading...

item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! For the FA Cup, the early rounds are the juice. The first round proper to be played out over the long weekend is looking, well, proper. And on Saturday at 3pm GMT, a proper time, 31 ties will kick off. No VAR, either. At the stage when the bottom two Football League divisions join the competition, focus remains on those non-league clubs fighting for the honour of the pyramid … John Aloisi winning or choking​ the Chinese Super League , a league so ‘super’ that nine of all 16 clubs in it started the season on negative points due to ‘match-fixing, gambling and corruption’ by the way, and the league leaders not even scoring a single goal in seven hours, is really not something to lay upon someone with a bad hangover. Apropos of nothing, if anyone has any objections to my views on the Chinese Super League, please address any correspondence to: Mr K Mbappé, Madrid (there’s no point two of us getting into trouble)” – Noble Francis. As a man of a certain age frequently being reminded of how out of date I am, the recent readers’ letters regarding technical solutions to shirt-pulling (Football Daily letters passim) concerns triggered distant memories. In late 1991 I was working in the Patents Advice Centre, Newcastle Central Library. A gentleman asked for help to possibly patent an ‘invention’: a football shirt with the seams held together by Velcro, so that any tug would ‘open’ the seam and provide clear evidence to the referee of illegal cloth gathering. As I helped him search for possible equivalent innovations in our paper database (yes kids!) we chatted amiably until I asked how he had come to this seemingly simple yet brilliant innovation. He paused, reddened and began to exhale with elevated pressure: ‘Did you see Arsenal the other night? Tony Adams? Disgraceful. It should never be allowed! In fact, with this shirt it won’t be, and Arsenal will have to learn to defend decently!’ Happy memories, obviously irrelavant to the modern game” – Garren Mulloy. Not fair! Bias! (Picture me, arms wide out, mouth open, eyebrows as high as they’ll go, appealing for reason.) I wrote about skin-tight shirts the other day and you ignored it, publishing a Velcro alternative. Now you’ve published another letter about skin-tight shirts ( yesterday’s letters ), days later. And it gets letter o’ the day! What’s the literary equivalent of kicking the keeper’s water bottle in frustration? I’ve just done that” – Ken Muir. I see that Celtic finally moved up the Bigger Vase charts on Thursday night and started playing a tune when their subs Osmand, Durán and Donovan came on. Too corny but my wife actually laughed at this” – Hugh Jamieson. That was a topsy-turvy Durán Durán show at Celtic, but what else would you expect from a bunch of Wild Bhoys?” – Peter Oh. item.title: ‘In moments of pain, football comes together’: Spain says goodbye to Jesús de Miguel
item.description: Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but the streets of Navahermosa were fuller yet quieter to mourn the Tenerife striker at his funeral The narrow streets of Navahermosa in La Mancha were fuller than they have ever been on Thursday afternoon and quieter too. Silence accompanied the funeral cortege as its made way from the funeral home to the parish church of San Miguel Arcángel carrying Jesús de Miguel Alameda, “Demi”, the Tenerife striker who died after an on-field collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono three days earlier. Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but now they were joined by the game he loved. “We wanted to be close to his parents, his wife and daughter. In moments of pain, football comes together more than ever,” said Luis de la Fuente. The Spain manager did not say much else; there was not much else he could say, not much anyone could. These have been dark, desperate days, days when it was impossible to assimilate what has happened, and there will be more. “We will get through this together but we will need help, professional help,” the Tenerife president, Felipe Miñambres, said. item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo merely the latest example of a great player who couldn’t let go | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There is no doubt his international career was an incredible one, but it would have been greater still if he had not lingered on the stage so long Nothing, perhaps, is quite so difficult for an elite sportsperson as timing their exit. It’s not easy for any person in any job to weigh the hope of having more to give with the desire not to linger beyond their usefulness, but it’s perhaps particularly hard for top athletes because unrealistic self-confidence is so essential to their success. It takes an almost unhealthy level of self-belief for anybody to make the sacrifices to get to the top, to dedicate themselves to such a precarious vocation, to overcome all the setbacks and injuries and failures. How can someone – whose whole life has been spent assuring themselves there are no odds they cannot overcome – accept that is it, that the time has come to say goodbye? The news that Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football brings with it, inevitably, a sadness. Sadness we will no longer see him skipping past a defender, or burying a neck-thrusting header, and sadness in that the end of the career of any great is a reminder of mortality; all things in time must pass. But there is also a sadness he timed his departure so badly. For at least three tournaments, there has been a sense of Ronaldo holding Portugal back. Continue reading...

item.title: Uefa faces political flashpoint over Sevastopol’s ascent in Russian football
item.description: Promotion to third tier for Crimean club would be clear violation of governing body’s rules amid conflict in Ukraine Uefa and Fifa face a decisive test of their appetite to punish Russia’s integration of teams from illegally occupied Ukrainian territory after FC Sevastopol, from Crimea, won promotion to the country’s professional third tier. Sevastopol were declared champions of group one in Football National League (FNL) 2B, in effect Russia’s fourth division, last month and are believed to have applied for a licence to compete at the level above. Should it be granted and they proceed to FNL 2A, it would appear a violation of Uefa rules that prohibit Crimean clubs from playing in competitions organised by the Russian Football Union (RFU). The governing body would come under severe pressure to extend sanctions on European football’s pariah state, whose club and national teams are banned from competing in international tournaments. item.title: Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or party gives way to anxiety-filled hangover for Bayern Munich | Andy Brassell
item.description: Dortmund did not read the script, remaining level on points with the defending champions at the top of the table It was the moment they had all been … not so much waiting for, but planning, pushing and yearning for. In the videos that announce the starting lineup on the giant scoreboard before kick-off, every Bayern Munich player turns to face the camera with their personal salute, greeting or goal celebration, the playful progression from the standard folding of arms. Except on Saturday evening, the No 9 turned around smiling, and cradling the golden trophy. In the midweek DFB Pokal stroll against Magdeburg there had been a salute, the players welcoming Harry Kane on to the pitch with a guard of honour to commemorate his Ballon d’Or victory two nights before. This, however, was the real party, the moment where the England captain’s and Bayern’s successful union and the apex it has reached was celebrated in front of a global audience. There was every reason to believe it would be a full and satisfying victory lap, even in Der Klassiker, with proper competition so often bringing the best out of the Rekordmeister. item.title: Folarin Balogun takes a first, tiny step toward moving on from a calamitous summer
item.description: The USMNT striker scored his first goal since the World Cup in a losing effort against Paris FC. Could it lead to something more? Before this weekend, the last time Folarin Balogun scored was in the United States’ 2-0 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina at this past summer’s World Cup. In the immediate aftermath, the outlook for Balogun seemed rosy; an ascendant player who could muster a goal in tense games. At half-time against Bosnia, US fans weren’t just wondering how far his team could advance – they were sizing Balogun up against some of the world’s best strikers. But for most of the ensuing four months, Balogun has been in limbo. His breakout World Cup was overshadowed by a red card in that same game against Bosnia and Herzegovina, followed by a scandal of which he wanted no part. Just as it seemed a summer move away from Monaco could get his club career on track, he broke off a possible deadline-day move to Everton after a lengthy visit to the training grounds and a medical he felt was improperly handled. item.description: Club’s predicament raises interesting questions about principles, both for individuals and the Premier League I felt unbelievably ponderous. My head was made of Aztec stone. I realised I didn’t want to be with all these people. Somebody came at me, a huge individual in silver and blue. I fell at his feet and grabbed one shoe. I started untying the lace. He kicked away from me. I got up and walked off. I was exceedingly hungry. Not my words. Also not the words of the Manchester City centre-back Marc Guéhi, despite what you were thinking there. This is instead a condensed quote from the mind of Gary Harkness, existentially curious college running-back and the narrator of Don DeLillo’s great American football novel End Zone. item.title: A phone-free Yellow Wall: are Dortmund urging fans to be present or policing them?
item.description: It makes sense that sports teams want to keep influencers out of their games. The battle some clubs are waging with their fans, however, is a different dilemma By all appearances, things on the Yellow Wall seemed as they always had been. The stadium announcer hollered out the first names of Borussia Dortmund’s starting lineup and the supporters responded with their last names, tens of thousands of voices bellowing as one. Dozens of black and yellow flags waved over Europe’s largest standing terrace, a mass of faces fixed on the field beneath them. And then Signal Iduna Park, sold out with 81,365 fans, roared when Max Beier’s lone goal led Dortmund to victory over Eintracht Frankfurt last Saturday, putting the home side even on points with Bayern Munich atop the Bundesliga standings. item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

item.description: Swindon manager has a history of viral outbursts but fans want a united club and manager they can support In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.” To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

And we’ll set you up for the weekend and let you know our live coverage plans so you’ll be ahead of the game. Here’s what you can expect from us. Try our other sports emails: there’s daily football news and gossip in The Fiver , and weekly catch-ups for cricket in The Spin and rugby union in The Breakdown . Living in Australia?
